title: Gross Amount of an Arrears Certain Installment on Ashgrove Income Annuity Period-Certain Contracts
content:
On an Income Annuities period-certain contract, the gross amount of an arrears installment — a certain installment that fell due after the annuitant's death and on or before the approval of the death claim and was never issued — depends on the cost-of-living history of the contract and on what is held in suspense for its payment date.

**Which installment.** The arrears installment is the one whose payment date follows the installments of that span already issued, counted from the first payment date after the death; "its payment date" below means that date. The payment dates follow the contract's installment frequency (every 1, 3, 6 or 12 months for monthly, quarterly, semiannual or annual).

## Rule

(a) **Cost-of-living increase since the annuitant's last installment.** Where the contract carries a cost-of-living rate, a cost-of-living increase has taken effect on a contract anniversary falling after the payment date of the last installment issued to the annuitant, and nothing is held in suspense for the arrears installment's payment date, the arrears installment is paid at the amount of that last installment raised by the cost-of-living rate once for each contract anniversary falling after its payment date and on or before the arrears installment's own payment date. The amount is rounded to the cent after each of the first twelve such increases, and any further increases are compounded in one step and rounded to the cent. Where no anniversary falls in that range, the amount is the last installment issued to the annuitant, unraised.

(b) **Amount held in suspense.** Where an amount is still held in suspense for the arrears installment's payment date — the held entries for that payment date less any releases recorded for it — the arrears installment is paid at that held amount.

(c) On any other contract neither of these rules applies.

"The last installment issued to the annuitant" is the issued installment with the latest payment date whose payee is the annuitant, as the contract's activity history shows it.

## Cases (hypothetical contract: cost-of-living rate 3%, contract anniversary 15 March, last installment issued to the annuitant $2,000.00 for 1 February)

| Arrears payment date | Held for that date | Anniversaries after 1 February up to the arrears date | Gross arrears installment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March, paid after 15 March | Nothing | 0 | $2,000.00 — rule (a), no increase yet by that date |
| 1 April | Nothing | 1 (15 March) | $2,060.00 — rule (a) |
| 1 April of the following year | Nothing | 2 | $2,060.00 raised by 3% is $2,121.80 — rule (a) |
| 1 April | $2,000.00 held | — | $2,000.00 — rule (b) |

A contract without a cost-of-living rate, or one on which no anniversary has fallen since the annuitant's last installment, and with nothing held for the arrears date, is outside both rules.

**Rounding beyond twelve increases (hypothetical).** Fourteen increases at 1% on $1,000.00: the amount is rounded to the cent after each of the first twelve, giving $1,126.84; the remaining two are applied together, $1,126.84 multiplied by 1.01 multiplied by 1.01 is $1,149.4895, rounded once to $1,149.49.
